title: Fix customers per status
prompt: This report should show how many orders and how many different customers each order status has, but `customers` always equals `orders`. Find the bug and fix `solve(orders)`.
rules: `orders` counts every row of the status, repeated rows included.
`customers` counts the different `customer_id` values with that status. A customer with three paid orders counts once for `paid`, and a missing id isn't counted.
Orders with a missing `status` form their own row. Return `status`, `orders` and `customers`.
hints: Compare the two aggregates. What does `F.count("customer_id")` count?
`F.count("col")` counts rows where the column isn't missing, so a customer with three orders counts three times.
You need an aggregate that counts each different value once. `F` has a "distinct" version of count.
explanation: `F.count("customer_id")` counts rows that have a customer id, so it equals `orders` whenever every order has a customer. Different customers are a distinct count: `F.countDistinct("customer_id").alias("customers")`. It counts each id once per group and skips missing ids. Keep `F.count("*")` for `orders`; switching that to a distinct count of `order_id` would hide repeated rows.
